# Records

[A `record` declaration takes the same form as a `struct`](#spec.declarations.records.legality-1):

```metel
record Handle {
    fd: i64,
    name: String,
}

fun main() {
    let h := Handle { fd = 3, name = "x".to_string() };
    assert(h.fd == 3);
}
```

A third declaration kind alongside `struct`, `enum` and `aspect`. `record X .{ ... }` is
accepted everywhere `struct X .{ ... }` is — same declaration grammar, same construction
syntax, same field access, same generic-parameter list, same aspect-impl coherence rules
— with exactly one difference: a `record`'s declared row is *structurally visible*, so
it satisfies row bounds ([Generics — Row bounds](../types/generics/row-bounds.md)) and
row-conditional impl resolution ([Generics — Open rows](../types/generics/open-rows.md)) the way a
plain `struct`'s row never does.

`std::core` provides field-wise `Clone` for a record when every field implements `Clone`.

The implementation recursively clones each field and preserves the record's type.
This does not add `Eq`, `Ord`, or `Hash`; those aspects remain governed by their
separate designs.

A `record` may take a `record`-kinded parameter, spliced as `..R` wherever the type is named; the
parameter stands for extra fields the user of the type supplies:

```metel
record Builder<record R> { name: String, data: .{ ..R } }

fun describe<record R>(b: Builder<..R>) -> String { b.name }

fun main() {
    let a := Builder { name = "a", data = .{ .retries = 3 } };
    let b := Builder { name = "b", data = .{ .auth = "t", .retries = 1 } };
    assert(describe(a) == "a");
    assert(describe(b) == "b");
}
```

Records of `Copy` fields are `Copy`, and records of `Display` fields are `Display`, through
`std::core` impls over `.{ ..R }` with `where ..R: Copy` and `where ..R: Display`
respectively ([Field-wise row constraints](../types/generics/field-wise-row-constraints.md)).

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.records.legality-1}

`record X { field: Type, ... }` is legal everywhere `struct X { field: Type, ... }` is,
with an identical declaration body grammar: the same field list, the same generic
parameter list (including a `record` type parameter used as a row), the same construction
syntax (including shorthand field init and the zero-field forms), and the same field
projection syntax as a `struct`'s own row.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.records.legality-2}

A `record`'s declared row is visible to structural matching: it satisfies a row bound
(`<record T: .{ ... }>`) and is matched by row-conditional impl resolution against its
*current* row — the row narrows as fields are moved out, exactly as it does
for a plain `struct`'s own (invisible) row. A plain `struct`'s row is never visible to
either mechanism, regardless of width — projecting every field a `struct` declares does
not earn it `record`'s eligibility, only an explicit `record` declaration does.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 6fecc8dcbfdd36500a77b2f6139e5f5ef970ce10 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.records.legality-3}

Changing a `struct` declaration to `record` (or vice versa) preserves the type's name,
brand, generic parameters and aspect impls unchanged; only the row's visibility to
structural matching changes. A whole-value call site typechecks identically before and
after the change in either direction. `struct` → `record` is additive for callers: it
newly makes the type satisfy row bounds and row-conditional impls it did not before.
`record` → `struct` is not: any caller holding a row bound or row-conditional impl
naming the type's fields stops typechecking, with no way to find every such caller from
the declaration site alone, since satisfaction is structural rather than declared.
`struct` → `record` also publishes every field, including ones that were module-private,
because every field of a `record` is public. Converting back gives each field the
`struct` default, module-private, so a field that must stay visible needs an explicit
`pub` again.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.records.legality-4}

Every field of a `record` declaration is public, and a record field carries no
visibility modifier: its fields are written bare. A `pub` written on a `record` field
is a compile error, reported at the modifier as a syntax error; the diagnostic names the
field and the record, says that every record field is public so the modifier is removed,
and points an author who wanted a private field at a `struct`. There is no way to make a
record field private. The rule applies to every `record`, generic or not, and never to a
`struct`.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->
